brief: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down effective immediately, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO while a permanent search proceeds. Analyst Timothy Arcuri flags three fallout channels: a likely near-term pause in Nvidia's AI financing deals, loss of Huang's edge in supply-chain procurement, and risk of tighter US export restrictions on NVDA and AMD shipments to China and beyond. NVDA fell as much as 14% intraday before recovering to -5%, and the market read the move as idiosyncratic rather than systemic, with AMD, AVGO and QCOM higher and hyperscalers up 1.1%. Separately, OpenAI is backing bipartisan congressional chip-export curbs on China, adding momentum after Huang's ouster, and Chinese AI hardware names sold off on the uncertainty. Trump's Truth Social post saying the US doesn't need an Iran deal shut down the Vance back-channel, spiked Brent, and pushed short yields and the 10-year (to 5.13%) higher, flattening the curve and lifting XLE. Hawkish Fedspeak from Williams, Daly, Goolsbee and Hammack reinforced a hiking bias, the yen breached 160 prompting a Japanese intervention warning, and Microsoft suffered a 10+ hour global outage.
